title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 45
paragraphs: On hearing this, they at once accompanied the men to the guard-posts; and when they had arrived, Alexander said to them: “Athenians, I entrust these words of mine to you as a deposit, charging you to keep them secret and tell them to no one except Pausanias, so that you may not bring me to ruin. For I would not utter them if I did not care greatly for the general safety of Greece, seeing that I am a Greek myself by original descent and would not wish to see Greece enslaved instead of free. I tell you, then, that Mardonius and his army cannot get the sacrifices to turn out as he wishes, otherwise you would long since have fought. Now, however, he has resolved to let the sacrifices alone and to bring on a battle at dawn; for, as I conjecture, he fears you may assemble in greater numbers. Therefore prepare yourselves. If Mardonius should after all put off the battle and not bring it on, stay where you are and hold out patiently, for they have provisions only for a few days remaining. And if this matter turns out according to your wish, each of you ought then to remember me too with regard to liberation, since I have done so hazardous a deed for the Greeks' sake out of zeal for you, wishing to reveal to you Mardonius's design so that the barbarians may not fall upon you unprepared. I am Alexander the Macedonian.” Having spoken, he rode back to the camp and to his own position.
